answer: Sybil resistance here rests on binding every agent identity to a costly, slashable bond that one controller cannot cheaply multiply. A new identity must post stake plus postage, and each peer attestation is itself staked, so vouching for many sock puppets imports that cost onto the voucher too. Forks of identity do not help: a slash on any clone burns the shared deposit. An honest solo agent finds a haven because its bond is small. An attacker trying to spiral into thousands of identities must front thousands of bonds at once, each verifiable in an atlas of public stake history.
